title: Finite Tate coefficients descend from pro-etale to etale sites
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizer $\varpi_F$, and $n\geq1$, and set $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme], and let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For every $r\geq1$ such that $\ell^rA=0$, set
$$A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(1)=\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$$
using the finite etale Tate sheaf of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For the finite-level pro-etale Tate sheaf $A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\nu_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1).$$
It identifies the tensor powers $\nu_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(a)$ with $A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(a)$ for all $a\geq0$, where powers and derived tensor have the conventions of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. These isomorphisms commute with scheme pullback and with the transition $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{r'-r}}$ when $r'\geq r$; in particular the etale sheaf and its comparison are canonically independent of the annihilating power. The etale descent with this comparison is unique up to the unique comparison-preserving isomorphism. No divisibility assumption on $n$ by the ramification index is required.

proof.text: Put $Z=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$, $C=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}$, $R_r=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$ and $L=\varprojlim_s\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$. The root projections are $p_r:L\to\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$. Clause (2) of lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free supplies the $C$-module structure of $L$ and its finite reduction $L\otimes_C R_r\cong\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$. The completed coefficient quotient theorem gives $C/\ell^rC\cong R_r$. Apply it to the Noetherian DVR $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $(\ell)$; these ring properties and $\mathbf Z_\ell/(\ell^r)=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ are in def-weil-l-adic-numbers. The finite reduction is the one belonging to the specified roots tower, induced by $p_r$. Thus it identifies $L/\ell^rL$ with $\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$. All these constructions are on the pro-etale site, and only $\ell$ invertible on $T$ is needed.

source.place: Finite Tate reduction of the roots tower; completed constant coefficient quotients, sites-modules.tex Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat

proof.text:
Reassociate the two coefficient tensors in def-coefficient-twists-detailed: $A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)\cong L\otimes_Z A_T$. The maps on local pure tensors are $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes ba$ and $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Since $\ell^rA=0$, tensoring with $A_T$ factors through $L/\ell^rL$: the inverse maps are $x\otimes a\mapsto\bar x\otimes a$ and $\bar x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes a$, independent of the lift because $(\ell^ry)\otimes a=y\otimes\ell^ra=0$. The sheaf tensor definition makes these sectionwise formulas descend after sheafification. Step 1 therefore gives the isomorphism
$$\theta_r:A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{R_r}A_T,\qquad x\otimes a\longmapsto p_r(x)\otimes a.$$
No flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; quotient tensor and reassociation by their explicit inverse pure-tensor maps

proof.text:
Apply lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections to the underlying etale root sheaf. For a weakly etale $f:W\to T$, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback identifies $f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$ with $\mu_{\ell^r,W}^{\mathrm{et}}$. Sections at $W$ are exactly units $z\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$ satisfying $z^{\ell^r}=1$, which is the defining value of the pro-etale root sheaf. This gives
$$c_r:\nu_T^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}.$$
Restriction is pullback of the same unit, so these objectwise bijections are natural. Powers give both the scalar actions and the transitions; hence $c_r$ is $R_r$-linear after the constant-ring identification of lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, and $c_r\nu_T^{-1}(z\mapsto z^{\ell^{r'-r}})=(z\mapsto z^{\ell^{r'-r}})c_{r'}$. This uses the section formula for all weakly etale $W$, without an affine or finite-type hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale; finite roots and their functoriality in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PK, section-kummer

proof.text:
The ringed-topos tensor comparison and the canonical identifications of the constant $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and $A$ sheaves give
$$\nu_T^*(\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r} A_T)\cong\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{R_r}A_T.$$
Here the mixed-coefficient tensor is the coequalizer imposing the $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$-balancing relations; the inverse image preserves this coequalizer and the integer tensor, and sends the scalar-action maps to the same scalar-action maps. Equivalently this is ordinary ringed pullback over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ followed by the $A$-action. Compose this comparison, denoted $c_r\otimes1$, with $\theta_r^{-1}$ from step 2. The resulting $A$-linear isomorphism $\beta_r=\theta_r^{-1}(c_r\otimes1)$ is the required $\nu_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(1)\cong A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$, normalized by the specified root projections and constant scalar maps.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; canonical comparison at finite discrete coefficients

proof.text:
For $r'\geq r$ let $P_{r',r}$ be the root power transition. The definition of the inverse limit gives $p_r=P_{r',r}p_{r'}$, so on every local generator $x\otimes a$ of $L\otimes_ZA_T$,
$$(P_{r',r}\otimes1)\theta_{r'}(x\otimes a)=p_r(x)\otimes a=\theta_r(x\otimes a).$$
Therefore $P_{r',r}\otimes1=\theta_r\theta_{r'}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. On the etale site the corresponding transition is an isomorphism by the last assertion of lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback. Step 3 identifies its pullback with $P_{r',r}\otimes1$, whence $\beta_r\nu_T^*(P_{r',r}\otimes1)=\beta_{r'}$. The power maps compose by multiplying their exponents; taking a common larger annihilating exponent compares any two choices and gives the cocycle identity. This proves canonical independence of $r$, including its comparison, rather than merely existence of an unspecified identification.

source.place: The root transition identity and tensor quotient normalization; section-comparison

proof.text:
Let $v:T'\to T$. Use the comparison square $\nu_{T'}^*v_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\cong v_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_T^*$ and the etale root pullback of lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback. The standard pro-etale root maps are compatible with the tower transitions by lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso (1)-(2). They induce a map from $v^{-1}L_T$ to $L_{T'}$ by taking the family $c^v_{\mu_{\ell^s}}v^{-1}p_s$ of projections; this uses the limit universal property, without asserting that inverse image preserves this infinite limit. Extend scalars to define the usual finite-level map $b_v:v^*A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)\to A_{T'}^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$. By the tensor comparison and constant-scalar identification, its $r$-th projection satisfies
$$\theta_{r,T'}b_v=(c^v_{\mu_{\ell^r}}\otimes1)\,v^*\theta_{r,T}.$$
Step 3's section description identifies the root map on the right with the etale root pullback through the comparison square: both pull a unit back to the same unit. Substitute $\beta_r=\theta_r^{-1}(c_r\otimes1)$ in this equation. It says precisely that $b_v$ agrees with the pullback of $\beta_r$ and the etale twist pullback isomorphism, so $b_v$ is an isomorphism and the claimed square commutes. Identity and composition compatibility follow by the same equation at the finite root projection and the identity/composition compatibility of the two cited pullback comparisons.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; root pullback and finite projection compatibility, with Tag 03EL tensor comparison

proof.text:
For $a=0$ use the constant-$A$ comparison, and define $ eta_{r,a}$ for $a>0$ by tensoring $a$ copies of $ eta_r$ and the canonical inverse-image tensor comparisons. Explicitly $ eta_{r,a+1}$ is $ eta_{r,a}\otimes_A eta_r$ after that tensor comparison. This is induction on the tensor-power definition in def-coefficient-twists-detailed and def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, so gives $
u_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(a)\cong A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(a)$. Steps 5 and 6 give the transition and scheme-pullback squares factor by factor; naturality of the tensor comparison gives their tensor powers. For derived tensors the ringed-topos derived tensor theorem supplies $L
u_T^*(K\otimes_A^LM)\cong L
u_T^*K\otimes_A^LL
u_T^*M$, and exactness of the finite-coefficient comparison identifies $L
u_T^*$ with the termwise $
u_T^*$. Thus the same comparisons respect the specified derived tensor conventions.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; derived version sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text:
Finally the comparison adjunction unit is invertible on all module sheaves by lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-unit, applied to $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, which is Grothendieck abelian by lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian. Hence $
u_T^*$ is fully faithful. If $G$ is another etale descent equipped with $\alpha:
u_T^*G\cong A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$, the map $\alpha^{-1} eta_r:
u_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(1)	o
u_T^*G$ lifts to exactly one etale map $h$. Its inverse lifts in the same way; faithfulness says their composites are identities. Thus $h$ is the unique comparison-preserving isomorphism. The argument applies to each tensor power as well. Throughout the finite reduction uses only $\ell^rA=0$, never $A$ flat over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ or $n$ a multiple of a ramification index. On the empty scheme all maps are the unique maps between zero module sheaves; at $a=0$ the comparison is the coefficient-ring identity.

theorem finite_tate_site_descent :
    ∃ b : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}), IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤)) →
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (hA : ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0) (k : ℕ),
      (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) T).obj
        (finiteEtaleTateTwist T (l ^ (r + 1)) _ hA k) ≅ finiteTateProSheaf l E n T k,
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤))) (r : ℕ)
      (hA : ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0) (k : ℕ),
      IsFiniteTateSiteComparison l E n T r hA k (b T hT r hA k)) ∧
    (∀ (T T' : Scheme.{u}) (v : T' ⟶ T)
      (hT : IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤))) (hT' : IsUnit (l : Γ(T', ⊤)))
      (r : ℕ) (hA : ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0) (k : ℕ),
      ∃ (c : (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) v).obj
          (finiteEtaleTateTwist T (l ^ (r + 1)) _ hA k) ≅
            finiteEtaleTateTwist T' (l ^ (r + 1)) _ hA k)
        (d : (ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) v).obj
          (finiteTateProSheaf l E n T k) ≅ finiteTateProSheaf l E n T' k),
      IsFiniteTateEtalePullback l E n T v r hA k c ∧
      IsFiniteTateProPullback l E n T v k d ∧
      (ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) v).mapIso
          (b T hT r hA k) ≪≫ d =
        (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) v).app
            (finiteEtaleTateTwist T (l ^ (r + 1)) _ hA k) ≪≫
        (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) T').mapIso c ≪≫ b T' hT' r hA k) ∧
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤))) (r r' : ℕ) (_h : r ≤ r')
      (hA : ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0)
      (hA' : ((l ^ (r' + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0) (k : ℕ),
      ∃! t : finiteEtaleTateTwist T (l ^ (r' + 1)) _ hA' k ≅
          finiteEtaleTateTwist T (l ^ (r + 1)) _ hA k,
        IsFiniteTateEtaleTransition l E n T r r' hA hA' k t ∧
        (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) T).mapIso t ≪≫ b T hT r hA k =
            b T hT r' hA' k) ∧
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤))) (r : ℕ)
      (hA : ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0) (k : ℕ)
      (G : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)))
      (alpha : (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) T).obj G ≅
          finiteTateProSheaf l E n T k),
      ∃! h : finiteEtaleTateTwist T (l ^ (r + 1)) _ hA k ≅ G,
        (ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (finiteTateCoefficient l E n)) T).mapIso h ≪≫ alpha =
            b T hT r hA k)
